basis: All four evidence commands re-run at 06d9f8ce and produced the quoted output byte-for-byte. I established the claim by an independent route: I read internal/domain/inventory/analytics_types.go:105-144 in full and confirmed every other money field in SellSheetItem carries the Cents suffix in both name and tag (BuyCostCents, CostBasisCents, CLValueCents, OverridePriceCents, ComputedPriceCents, AISuggestedPriceCents), so the five are the sole exceptions inside their own structs. I then widened the sweep repo-wide with `git grep -nE '^\s+[A-Za-z0-9]+\s+(int|int64)\s+`json:"[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*(Price|Cost|Value|Profit|Revenue|Basis|Total)[a-zA-Z0-9]*"' 06d9f8ce -- 'internal/*.go' 'internal/**/*.go' | grep -v _test.go | grep -viE 'Cents"|Usd"|USD"|Pct"|Count"'` — ten hits, of which five are these fields and the other five (noValue, unsoldTotal, withCLValue, compsAboveCost, clPricedCards) are counts, not money. So across every int money JSON tag in internal/, these five are the complete exception set to a repo-wide unit-suffix convention. Denomination confirmed as cents independently: service_sell_sheet.go:48 assigns snapshot.ConservativeCents, :55 assigns purchase.CLValueCents, :82 copies TargetSellPrice into ComputedPriceCents, :176 accumulates item.CostBasisCents. Zero-consumer claim confirmed: web/ grep returns only the five type declarations, and web/src/react/utils/sellSheetHelpers.tsx (the one helper naming SellSheetItem) reads none of them.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Evidence claim 4 overstates the convention. The finding argues an unsuffixed JSON field 'actively asserts the wrong unit' because CLAUDE.md:194 says API responses use USD. That does not hold at this baseline: the repo emits cents over the wire pervasively with a Cents tag suffix, and the handful of genuinely-USD API fields carry their own explicit suffix (campaigns_analytics.go:68-69 spendUSD/capUSD from `float64(d.SpendCents) / 100.0`; analytics_types.go:202-203 overrideTotalUsd/suggestionTotalUsd). The real convention is 'the suffix carries the unit', so these five fields record no unit anywhere rather than asserting dollars. Severity lowered to low on that basis plus the finding's own concession that no consumer reads the fields, so there is no live defect — this is a latent hazard for the next consumer, not a bug. The defect itself, and the exhaustiveness of the exception set, are confirmed.

basis: All three evidence commands reproduce. I re-derived the producer independently by reading internal/domain/portfolio/service.go:225-262 rather than the finding's quoted window: the switch at :242 buckets both inventory.SaleChannelEbay and inventory.SaleChannelTCGPlayer into bucket.marketplaceRevenue / bucket.marketplaceNetProfit, and the ratio computed from those two locals is assigned to CampaignHealth.EbayChannelMarginPct at :257. The name is therefore factually wrong about which channels it covers, not merely inelegant. The section comment above the declaration (health_types.go:36-37) independently confirms the intended concept is 'marketplace margin', not eBay. Propagation confirmed at eight non-test sites; the misnomer additionally reaches a user-visible string — service.go:128-131 and snapshot.go:138-141 format the value into a health reason, and those two sites already say 'marketplace channels profitable', so the prose and the identifier disagree at the same call site.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The finding accepted the declaration comment's premise that the JSON name is 'retained for frontend compatibility' and preserved the tag on that basis. That premise is unverified and appears false at this baseline: `git grep -nE 'EbayChannelMarginPct|ebayChannelMarginPct' 06d9f8ce` over all tracked files returns hits only in internal/domain/{inventory,portfolio} Go files — no web/ consumer of the JSON field exists. Keeping the tag is still the conservative fix and costs nothing, but the fixer should know the compatibility constraint is not evidenced, and the comment asserting it is itself stale. Does not change severity.

I checked the obvious relocation target and it is gone too: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 06d9f8ce -- internal/platform` shows no internal/platform/cache package at all (only canonjson, cardutil, config, crypto, resilience, storage, telemetry). So the doc comment documents an interface, a usage example, and a TTL policy table for a type that exists nowhere. CLAUDE.md:58 repeats the claim, confirmed. what_the_finding_got_wrong: Acceptance criterion 3 is not satisfiable as written. It requires `git grep -n 'domain/storage'` to return nothing outside migration comments and audit run directories, but the string also appears at .claude/skills/polish-all/SKILL.md:45, docs/polish-progress.json:7, and docs/specs/2026-08-07-codebase-tech-debt-audit-design.md:118 — none of which are audit run directories. The controller should widen that criterion to the CLAUDE.md line plus the package path itself, or a fixer will read the ticket as unfinishable. The substantive claim is unaffected.

basis: All five evidence commands reproduce with the quoted output. I re-derived the width by reading the full `type Service interface` block in internal/domain/auth/service.go: 20 methods under six section comments (OAuth flow 6, session management 4, user management 3, token storage 1, email allowlist 4, admin 2). The concrete cost is real and I confirmed each leg by my own route. Two production implementations: internal/domain/auth/service_impl.go (*authService) and internal/adapters/clients/google/oauth.go (*OAuthService), the latter carrying an explicit `var _ auth.Service = (*OAuthService)(nil)` at oauth.go:83 and defining all 20 methods (counted 20 `^func (s *OAuthService)` in that file) — so SIZE-001's acceptance criterion 3 names a compile-time assertion that genuinely exists today and will genuinely detect the failure mode it targets. Three inline mockAuthService declarations at 20/20/22 methods, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 06d9f8ce -- internal/testutil/mocks | grep -i auth` returns only auth_inmemory.go and auth_repository.go, confirming no shared auth.Service mock exists and that the inline mocks breach the CLAUDE.md rule the finding cites. Narrow-consumer claim holds: scheduler 2/20, middleware 2/20, admin handler 4/20.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: One overstatement in evidence claim 3's parenthetical. It characterizes the three inline mocks as stubbing 20 methods 'to exercise 2, 2 and 4 real methods respectively' and generalizes to '18 no-op stub methods written three times over'. That is right for middleware/auth_test.go and scheduler/session_cleanup_test.go, but handlers/auth_test.go covers handlers/auth.go, which calls 11 of the 20 (`git grep -ohE 'h\.authService\.[A-Za-z]+' 06d9f8ce -- internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/auth.go | sort -u`: ConsumeOAuthState, CreateSession, DeleteSession, ExchangeCodeForTokens, GetLoginURL, GetOrCreateUser, GetUserInfo, IsEmailAllowed, SetUserAdmin, StoreOAuthState, StoreTokens). So that file carries 9 no-op stubs, not 18. The headline claim — no consumer in the repo uses the interface as a whole, maximum is 11 of 20 — survives, and the proposed narrow seams for the scheduler, middleware and admin handler are unaffected. The fixer should expect the auth handler to keep a wide seam.

basis: I read scripts/check-file-size.sh in full at 06d9f8ce rather than grepping it.
